title: Atmosphere layers & composition
examples: Which layer of the atmosphere is where most weather happens?
What gases make up the air we breathe?
Why is the ozone layer so important to life on Earth?

explain.say: The atmosphere has several layers stacked on top of each other.
The troposphere is the lowest layer and is where most of our weather happens.
The stratosphere above contains the ozone layer which protects us from UV rays.
The mesosphere is the middle layer where most incoming space rocks burn up.
The thermosphere is the highest layer where you can see the aurora lights.
The main gases in our atmosphere are nitrogen, oxygen, and argon.

faq.q: Why is the ozone layer so important for life?
faq.a: The ozone layer absorbs most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation. It prevents this radiation from reaching the Earth's surface in dangerous amounts.
asks: What does the ozone layer block?
How does ozone protect us from space?
Is the ozone layer necessary for humans?

faq.q: Which layer is the warmest, the mesosphere or the thermosphere?
faq.a: The thermosphere actually gets very hot due to high energy absorption. However, the temperature changes rapidly in these upper layers.
asks: Where is the hottest part of the air?
Does heat increase steadily through the layers?
What layer has the highest temperature?

faq.q: Are all the gases in the atmosphere mixed equally?
faq.a: No, the gases are mixed but some are much more abundant than others. Nitrogen is the most plentiful gas by far.
asks: Do we have equal amounts of oxygen and nitrogen?
What gas is the most common in the air?

faq.q: What happens to meteors when they hit the mesosphere?
faq.a: When meteors enter the mesosphere, the friction with the air causes them to heat up and burn up. This is what we often see as shooting stars.
asks: Why do we see bright streaks at night?
What layer burns up space rocks?
How do meteors disappear in the air?

faq.q: Does weather happen in the thermosphere?
faq.a: No, the weather we experience, like clouds and rain, happens in the lowest layer, the troposphere. The upper layers are too thin for typical weather.
asks: What layer has the most weather?

facts: The troposphere contains nearly all of the atmosphere's mass.
The ozone layer is primarily located in the stratosphere.
Nitrogen gas makes up approximately seventy-eight percent of the atmosphere.
The mesosphere is known for burning up most space debris.

quiz.say: If you are studying cloud formation and rain, which layer are you in?
quiz.show: Cloud formation and rain happen in the:
quiz.why: The troposphere is the lowest layer where most weather phenomena occur.

wrong.0: This layer is too high up to experience typical weather like rain.
wrong.2: This layer is mainly known for containing the ozone layer, not daily weather.
wrong.3: The mesosphere is where space rocks burn up, not where clouds form.

quiz.say: Which gas is the most abundant component of Earth's air?
quiz.why: Nitrogen gas is the most plentiful gas, making up about seventy-eight percent of the air.

wrong.0: Argon is a noble gas, but it is much less common than nitrogen.
wrong.1: Water vapor is variable and not the primary component listed.
wrong.3: Oxygen is very important, but it only makes up about twenty-one percent.

quiz.show: UV protection layer is in the:
quiz.why: The stratosphere is specifically named for containing the vital ozone layer.

wrong.1: While important, the troposphere is more about weather patterns.
wrong.2: The mesosphere's main role is burning up incoming space objects.
wrong.3: The thermosphere is too high up to be the primary location for ozone.
